prompt.context: The client, Echo Yankee Games (EYG), has approached the firm to help them boost profitability. EYG is a mobile gaming development agency that makes game applications for the iOS and Android platforms and has four genres of games: Trivia, Action, Puzzle, and Word games. In the last few years, they have done well financially, but still want to increase profitability.
prompt.question: What should Echo Yankee Games consider to improve their profitability?

clarifying_info.q: What does the competitive landscape look like?
clarifying_info.a: The market is extremely fragmented with no clear leaders.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a specific revenue or cost target?
clarifying_info.a: There is no specific revenue or cost target.
Revenue comes from two streams: in-app purchases and downloads.

framework: 1. Revenue: (a) Number of users — core demographic is children, consider growth/trends; (b) Price per user — in-app purchases and app downloads; (c) Product mix / high performers — Action, Trivia, Puzzle, Word
2. Costs: (a) Fixed — development, marketing; (b) Variable — server costs
3. Overall market: (a) Competitive landscape and competitive response; (b) Industry benchmarks

questions.prompt: EYG's current profit margins by game genre are Trivia 10%, Action 20%, Puzzle 30%, and Word 20%. The CMO says that by optimizing marketing efforts they can double the profit margins on any genre. By how much will EYG increase overall profit margins if they double the profit margin of Trivia games?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute the weighted average profit margin before and after doubling Trivia's margin, using the profit mix weights (Trivia 20%, Action 50%, Puzzle 20%, Word 10%). A strong candidate will also note that doubling Action games (the largest profit contributor at 50%) would yield a much greater improvement — from 20% to 30% overall.

math.setup: Weighted overall margin = sum of (genre margin * genre profit share). Genre profit shares: Trivia 20%, Action 50%, Puzzle 20%, Word 10%. Current margins: Trivia 10%, Action 20%, Puzzle 30%, Word 20%.
steps: After doubling Trivia margin to 20%: New overall = 20%*20% + 20%*50% + 30%*20% + 20%*10% = 4% + 10% + 6% + 2% = 22%
Bonus: Doubling Action margin to 40% instead: 10%*20% + 40%*50% + 30%*20% + 20%*10% = 2% + 20% + 6% + 2% = 30%; increase = 10 percentage points
math.answer: Overall profit margin increases by 2 percentage points (from 20% to 22%). Doubling Action games would be far more impactful, raising overall margin from 20% to 30%.

questions.prompt: EYG needs to sell 40,000 downloads to break even on developing an action game in one year. The core demographic (children) primarily plays in summer. On high-volume days a game is downloaded 300 times per day; during the school year it is downloaded 50 times per day. The app store is down for maintenance 65 days per year. How many high-volume days in one year does EYG need to break even on this action game?
questions.guidance: Candidate should set up a system of two equations with two unknowns (H = high-volume days, L = low-volume days), use the total available days (365 - 65 = 300 operating days) and the download target. A strong candidate will check feasibility: 100 high-volume days exceeds most summer breaks (~90 days), so the game is unlikely to break even in year one.

math.setup: H = high-volume days, L = low-volume days. Operating days = 365 - 65 = 300. Two equations: (1) 300H + 50L = 40,000; (2) H + L = 300.
steps: Feasibility check: 100 high-volume days > typical summer (~90 days), so break-even in year 1 is unlikely.
math.answer: H = 100 high-volume days. Since most summers are under 90 days, a new action game is not likely to break even in the first year.

questions.prompt: EYG's marketing team found they can acquire each new user for $4.00 via ads on other free-to-play games. These users spend $2.00 per year on in-game purchases on average. Should EYG use this marketing campaign?
questions.guidance: Candidate must apply the Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) formula. Variable costs can be assumed zero so all $2 revenue is profit. With i = 10% and r = 55%, CLV is positive but less than the $4 acquisition cost, so the campaign is not worthwhile. A strong candidate will brainstorm ways to improve retention or reduce acquisition cost. Bonus: calculate the break-even retention rate (~75%).

math.setup: CLV formula: CLV = m * (r / (1 + i - r)) - AC, where m = annual margin per user = $2, r = retention rate = 55% = 0.55, i = discount rate = 10% = 0.10, AC = acquisition cost = $4.
steps: Conclusion: Negative CLV; acquisition cost exceeds lifetime value by $2 per user.
math.answer: No. CLV = -$2 per user; the retention rate (55%) is too low. Break-even retention rate is approximately 73-75%.

brainstorming.prompt: Brainstorm ways EYG could improve user retention rate to make the marketing campaign viable.

categories.name: Product improvements
ideas: Add new levels and content updates to extend game life
Introduce social/multiplayer features to increase stickiness
Improve onboarding to reduce early drop-off

categories.name: Monetization & engagement
ideas: Daily login rewards and streak incentives
Push notifications to re-engage lapsed players

categories.name: Community & loyalty
ideas: Loyalty program or VIP tiers for frequent spenders
In-game clubs or guilds for social bonding

categories.name: Acquisition targeting
ideas: Better user targeting to acquire higher-quality users
A/B test ad creatives to attract users with higher inherent retention
Focus ads on genres with historically better retention (e.g., Puzzle)

recommendation: Focus on increasing profitability in the Action genre, which represents 50% of all profits — doubling its margin raises company-wide margin by 10 percentage points
Proceed with developing the proposed new action game but monitor download trajectory against the 100-day high-volume requirement
Do not launch the current marketing campaign unless CLV can be improved (raise retention rate to ~75%+ or lower acquisition costs below ~$2)
risks: Many assumptions were made around expected users and expected spend per user
Mobile platforms change rapidly and development teams must be able to pivot
Players can quickly lose interest in a game, compressing the effective CLV horizon
Other market players could respond to EYG's growth moves in the fragmented market
next_steps: Ensure the dev team has a clear roadmap for the new action game
Re-analyze assumption numbers (retention, spend/user) with real cohort data
Re-work the marketing plan to target higher-retention user segments or negotiate lower CPIs
Explore expansion into adjacent genres or platforms to diversify revenue
